text: What do you bring to the table? When I hear a man ask women that question, it already tells me about that man everything I need to know. So let me just clarify something here. Women sacrifice so much in relationships. Giving birth, raising children, putting dreams on hold, carrying the emotional weight, holding the home together, while still showing up with love. Women pour from empty cups day after day. So here's the question nobody likes to ask out loud. What can a man sacrifice for a woman? See, this is what I call twisting the meaning, changing the whole point of the discussion to paint men in a bad light. When guys ask, what do you bring to the table? They're not asking women who are good partners. They're not talking about the women who raise kids, build a home, support their men, and make sacrifices. Those women clearly bring a lot to the table, and most men respect them deeply. But let's be honest, that's not the majority. Most women today who are in the relationships aren't giving birth, raising multiple kids, or putting their careers on hold. Maybe in a marriage, more women do. But even then, we are living in a time with the lowest birth rates in modern history. So let's stop pretending that every woman is out there sacrificing everything for love and family. And even in the scenario she described, let's say a woman is raising kids and supporting her family. Great, but what about the man? He's probably working 10-12 hours a day, taking care of financial responsibilities, protecting the family, fixing things, solving problems, and still being expected to stay strong through it all. He sacrifices sleep, time, peace of mind, and years of his life to provide for his family. But somehow, that's invisible, and that's the manipulation right here, framing it as if only women give and men just take, when in reality, in most healthy relationships, both sides give a lot. The truth is, when men ask, what do you bring to the table? They are talking about the women who don't contribute anything. The ones who expect everything to be handed to them just for existing. The ones who think that showing up is enough. If you are a woman who actually puts effort, builds with her man, shows empathy, and brings peace, few men would question your value. But if all you offer is attitude and expectations, don't be surprised when someone asks, what do you bring to the table?
